title: install --force into a project never removes a file devbin stopped shipping, and once the manifest drops it no upgrade will: a retired lib/cmd/<name> goes on dispatching
body:
FOUND 2026-09-23 while building 0123, and asked for by vc as 0123's class in a project rather than an install. Driven by cc at 4c9d5a7.

WHAT HAPPENS. `bin/devbin install --into <project> --force` re-vendors devbin's half. It copies every file the source ships over what is there, and deletes nothing. A file the source has stopped shipping stays in the project's bin/.devbin/lib/, and the rewritten manifest no longer lists it. install.md:37 states this as the flag's behaviour.

DRIVEN, in a fixture. The source ships a handler at lib/cmd/which, a project is vendored from it with `which` enabled, and the source then retires the handler:
- Before the retirement, `bin/devbin which` runs devbin's handler.
- `install --into <project> --force` from the retired source exits 0, vendoring 60 files. The handler is still on disk, and the manifest no longer lists it.
- `bin/devbin which` still runs the retired handler. Dispatch reaches devbin's lib/cmd/ tier of D2 whether or not any manifest lists the file.
- A later `upgrade --from` the same source reports "Already up to date", 0 removed. upgrade retires an intact file the manifest lists and the source no longer ships. Once install --force has dropped the file from the manifest it is unlisted, and upgrade never removes an unlisted file.
- doctor notes it among "unowned files under bin/.devbin/lib", as a note rather than a failure.
- THE CONTRAST: in a second project vendored from the same source, a plain `upgrade --from` after the retirement removes it, printing "removed bin/.devbin/lib/cmd/which (no longer shipped)".

So the flag that exists to put devbin's half back in order is the one path that leaves a retired file in place for good, and a retired handler goes on answering its name.

THE FIX (vc, 2026-09-23): build on 0123's removal. 0123 makes publish_install remove what the install holds under bin/.devbin/lib/ and the source no longer ships, naming each removal. That removal becomes one function, with two callers: publish, and install's vendor mode. Each names what it removes, as publish now does. The build has to decide one question and say why: whether a retired file the PROJECT EDITED is removed too. install --force already overwrites edits without naming them (install.md:37), which argues for removing it. upgrade instead RELEASES an edited orphan rather than deleting it, which argues for keeping it and naming it. install.md:37 changes with the fix. It ships in 0.1.8, under hv's ruling, and lands with or after 0123 and 0127.

## Resolution

Fixed at c585f3d, in 0123's commit. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. A re-vendor, install --force into a project, retires each file the previous manifest recorded that the source no longer ships, and names each one. It does so edited or not, since --force already copies over edits. A file no manifest recorded is left alone, since it may be the project's own, and doctor names it. Nothing outside bin/.devbin/lib/, and nothing through a `..` segment, is touched. install.md's --force paragraph says so.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. The retirement arms were red at 0113's landing. The unrecorded-file and path-guard arms pass there by construction, since nothing was removed then, so mutants prove them. W1-W5 were killed: the candidates widened to every file on disk, the path guard dropped, only its `..` branch dropped, the removal deleted, and the pruning deleted.
- THE SUITE. As 0123's resolution: 1..1694, 1694 ok, 0 not ok, 5 expected skips, rc 0.
